rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a thermal pre-oxidation treatment to form an oxide layer, while the target uses nanoindentation/friction simulation at different temperatures without any pre-treatment. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (experimental coating treatment vs. simulation of mechanical testing).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature wear testing at 600-800°C with sliding/abrasive loads, whereas the target uses nanoindentation and friction simulation at 300-1200 K (27-927°C) with a specific loading/unloading protocol. The temperature ranges overlap partially, but the testing methods and specific conditions are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a protective oxide scale as the wear-resistance mechanism, while the target's mechanism is based on lattice disorder, dislocation density evolution, and a shift from stacking faults to lattice softening. These are contradictory mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced wear with pre-oxidation, while the target predicts stable wear resistance up to 600 K then a sharp decrease above 900 K. The predicted trends are opposite in direction regarding the effect of high temperature on wear resistance.
